newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong airport open despite heavy rains.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong airport open despite heavy rains.

text.p: Chinese President Jiang Zemin and other mainland VIPs will be able to fly out of Hong Kong on Tuesday despite driving rain and a severe rainstorm warning.
Richard Siegel, director of Hong Kong's Civil Aviation Department, said Kai Tak airport was open and operational "within the constraints of the weather".
Early on Tuesday, the Hong Kong Observatory warned the public to stay indoors and avoid travelling, saying more than 100 millimetres (four inches) of rain had fallen in a two-hour period.
Jiang and other Chinese officials were due to leave Hong Kong for Beijing on Tuesday morning after attending ceremonies marking Hong Kong's handover to Chinese rule at midnight (1600 GMT) on June 30.
